Occurrences.Kwic: 見境心不起名不生。不生即不滅。既無生滅即不被前塵所縛。當處解脫。不生名無念。無念即無滅。無念即無縛。無念即無脫。舉要而言。識心即離念。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (景德傳燈錄). Baotang Wuzhu owns the exact clause in the complete case.

Occurrences.Kwic: 知心與境本不相到，當處解脫。一一諸法，當處寂滅，當處道場。又本有之性，不可名目。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (百丈懷海禪師廣錄（四家語錄卷三）). Baizhang Huaihai owns the exact clause in the complete case.

Occurrences.Kwic: 榑桑不遠。莫向外馳求。當處發生。隨處自現。乾坤大地。皎皎明白。

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問：和尚不使沙彌童行，何得自燒？師撫掌三下。後僧舉似曹山，山云：一等是箇拍手撫掌，就中西園奇怪，俱胝一指頭禪，蓋謂承當處不諦當。

Occurrences.Kwic: 盡十方世界是箇無孔鐵鎚，迦葉不知。無汝擬議處，無汝承當處
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (續燈正統). Shimen Zhenjue Yuanweng Xin owns the exact clause in the complete case.

Senses.Explanation: at the very place concerned. Chan records repeatedly couple it with results said to occur without going elsewhere: liberation 'right where it is,' arising right there and appearing wherever one goes, quiescence right there, and the place of teaching right there. In public exchanges it also retains its direct locative force: when a visitor quotes 'without leaving the very place, constantly clear,' the identified master is asked where that is. Another discourse asks how one recognizes the buddhas and immediately surpasses them right there. These predicates and questions load an ordinary locative expression within Chan discourse.
